sources.words: Storm flow to be passed to full treatment
Average daily flow | Value: 120,000 | Unit: m³/day
Peak hourly flow (design) | Value: 7,500 | Unit: m³/h
The hydraulic profile shall accommodate the flows in Table 2-6 without surcharge of any structure and without reliance on pumped bypass.
Bidders shall design to the figures stated in Volume II. Volume II Clause 4.2 applies.

entry.gap: 'Dry weather flow' is not defined. If it equals the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, i.e. 5,000 m³/h), the storm flow to be passed to full treatment (3 x DWF, 15,000 m³/h) is twice the peak hourly design flow of 7,500 m³/h used for the hydraulic profile and the transmission main (VOL-II 4.1, 5.2), so the governing storm design flow is unclear.
entry.already_settled: ADD-02 Q11 settles that Bidders design to the Volume II figures: the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day) and peak hourly flow (7,500 m³/h, a peaking factor of 1.5 on the 5,000 m³/h average) stand, are not contradictory and are not re-asked. Q11 did not address row 2-6.4 or define DWF; VOL-II 4.2 itself asks Bidders to raise flow inconsistencies under VOL-I 5.1.
entry.practical_impact: Sets the hydraulic capacity of the inlet works, treatment streams and channels and possibly of the transmission main and reservoir; a two-fold difference in storm design flow is a major capex and footprint item and bears on meeting Table 2-4 under storm conditions.
entry.proposed_question: Volume II, Table 2-6, row 2-6.4, page 4: How is 'dry weather flow' in row 2-6.4 defined, and what storm flow, in m³/h, is to be passed to full treatment and accommodated by the hydraulic profile under Clause 4.1 (page 3), given that three times a dry weather flow equal to the average daily flow in row 2-6.1 (120,000 m³/day) would exceed the peak hourly flow (design) of 7,500 m³/h in row 2-6.2?
entry.interim_handling: Design to the stated Table 2-6 figures and carry the more onerous reading (3 x average daily flow, 15,000 m³/h, through inlet works and full treatment) as the hydraulic case, with the 7,500 m³/h case costed as a variant. Record the assumption in the design basis; add no qualification to the Proposal.

entry.topic: missing technical/contractual references (Volume III, Drawing 03-C-114, tie-in points)

sources.words: between the Facility outlet chamber and the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114
a minimum residual head of 15 m at the delivery point
at the two designated tie-in points
No claim arising from an alleged omission shall be entertained after the Proposal Due Date.

entry.gap: Volume III (Drawings), listed as an RFP Document, has not been issued. The effluent delivery point is identified only by Drawing 03-C-114, and the 'two designated tie-in points' to the collection network are not identified in any document issued.
entry.practical_impact: The delivery point fixes the route and length of the approximately 18 km main and the pumping head for 15 m residual head (VOL-II 5.2), which is also an Unavailability Event test (VOL-V 31.1(c)); the tie-in points fix the interface and temporary works (VOL-II 1.3). Omission claims close at the Proposal Due Date (VOL-I 3.4).
entry.proposed_question: Volume II, Clause 5.1, page 4, and Clause 1.3, page 2: Volume I Clause 3.1 (page 2) lists Volume III (Drawings) as an RFP Document, but Volume III has not been issued. Will the Authority issue Volume III or, failing that, state the location and ground level of the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114 and the location of the two designated tie-in points referred to in Clause 1.3?
entry.interim_handling: Design and price the main on the stated parameters (about 18 km, minimum DN1200, maximum 2.0 m/s, 15 m residual head) with the delivery point, route and tie-in locations as labelled assumptions and a cost allowance; completing the bid does not depend on receiving Volume III.

entry.topic: permit/table interpretation (rolling averages in the 30-day reliability run)

sources.words: PCOD shall not be certified until the Facility has completed a continuous reliability run of thirty (30) days at not less than 90% of nominal capacity, during which every parameter in Table 2-4 has been met.
A failure of any Table 2-4 parameter during the reliability run shall restart the run in full.
compliance assessed as a 30-day rolling average unless stated
delay liquidated damages at the rate of SAR 180,000 for each day of delay

entry.gap: Most Table 2-4 parameters are assessed as 30-day rolling averages, but VOL-II 7.2-7.3 do not say how such a parameter is 'met', or what counts as 'a failure', within a 30-day run: an average over the run, a daily rolling value using pre-run data, or individual samples.
entry.practical_impact: A failure restarts the full 30 days; PCOD timing drives delay liquidated damages of SAR 180,000 per day (VOL-V 18.1) and the 365-day termination right (VOL-V 18.3), so the commissioning programme and float depend on the answer.
entry.proposed_question: Volume II, Clauses 7.2 and 7.3, page 4: For Table 2-4 parameters whose basis of assessment is a 30-day rolling average, how is compliance determined during the 30-day reliability run (in particular, is the rolling average calculated over the run period only, or for each day of the run using data from before it began), and what constitutes 'a failure' of such a parameter for the purposes of Clause 7.3?
entry.interim_handling: Plan commissioning so that individual samples meet the rolling-average limits before the run starts, and hold programme float for at least one full restart; record this as a programme assumption.

entry.clause: Section 3, Note (3) to revised Table 1-1 (with Volume I Clauses 11.2 and 11.3)

sources.words: Marks are awarded on the Authority's standard five-point scale and multiplied by the weight shown.
is amended to sixty-five per cent (65%) technical and thirty-five per cent (35%) commercial.
A Proposal scoring less than seventy (70) marks out of one hundred (100) at the technical evaluation shall not proceed to commercial evaluation

entry.gap: Note (3) introduces 'the Authority's standard five-point scale' multiplied by 'the weight shown', but the scale is not in the pack and the revised table shows marks, not weights, so how a criterion score becomes marks out of 100 (and is tested against the 70-mark threshold) is not stated. No method is given anywhere for calculating the commercial score.
entry.already_settled: ADD-02 note (2) sets the weighting at 65% technical / 35% commercial, replacing VOL-I 11.2 (60/40); the minutes' 'seventy / thirty' remark does not bind (ADD-01 3.2). Note (1) keeps the 70-mark threshold, and the revised marks (B 15, D 20, total 100) are settled.
entry.practical_impact: Determines how the technical narrative is weighted across criteria, the margin needed above the 70-mark threshold (below it Envelope B is returned unopened, VOL-I 11.3), and how price translates into the 35% commercial score.
entry.proposed_question: Addendum No. 2, Section 3, Note (3) to revised Table 1-1, page 1: (a) What is the Authority's standard five-point scale, and how is a score on that scale converted into the marks shown in revised Table 1-1, including for the 70-mark threshold in Volume I Clause 11.3 (page 5), given that the table shows marks rather than weights? (b) By what method is the commercial score calculated for the 35% commercial weighting?
entry.interim_handling: Write to the revised marks per criterion (A 25, B 15, C 20, D 20, E 10, F 10) and aim for a clear margin above 70; treat the commercial formula as unknown and test price sensitivity without assuming one.
